Thank you very much, uh, Tanja, uh, Slovenia, uh, then I have the honor of giving the floor to Indonesia, to be followed by, um, by Chile, and that is, uh, Vice Minister Nasir, please, Indonesia.

Thank you, uh, thank you, co-chair, I will, I will follow the suggestion of, uh, of Minister Aspin, uh, that we should focus on how to move forward on the two state solution. Thank you very much, Indonesia. And let me just say from the chairs that I much appreciate this sharing experiences. This was also mentioned from Ireland and from Austria. Excellencies, delegates, Chile welcomes this meeting and the Global Alliance focus on moving from consensus to implementation. Our immediate priorities are clear, a sustained ceasefire, the release of all hostages, unhindered humanitarian access throughout Gaza, and full protection of civilians and essential infrastructure in accordance with international humanitarian law. We reaffirm our support to UNRWA and urge sustained financing for its essential neutral work. In the occupied West Bank, settlement expansion and settler violence violate international law and erode the viability of two states. They must cease. We stand ready to work with all partners to make this roadmap a reality now. Thank you very much.

Gracias, Chile. Gracias, Alberto. And then we'll give the floor to His Excellency Maxime Prevost, the Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Belgium, to be followed by the EU Commission. So Belgium, please.

Thank you, Excellencies, colleagues. First, let me thank Norway, Saudi Arabia, and the EU for organizing this important meeting. Earlier this week, we launched the New York Declaration. This commitment must now be matched by action. While our immediate priority remains the humanitarian situation, we must also seize the momentum and work together to support the Palestinian Authority in its efforts towards state and institution building. Peace entails the recognition of each other's rights, pain, narratives, and humanity. That's why we must invest in people-to-people programs. Dialogue, education, and shared experiences are essential to overcome decades of conflict, build trust between Palestinians and Israelis, and force the coexistence. Belgium has been a committed partner since 1997 through Enabel, our development agency. We've invested over 200 million in bilateral support and 600 million via the United Nations, civil society, and international organizations. Our focus includes education, local governance, and sustainable development. We have also invested in revitalizing historical city centers, promoting local businesses and tourism, and economic development, including in Sebastia, Area C, in the West Bank and East Jerusalem. Few donors have taken this approach, but if we believe in a two-state solution, we must invest where it matters. However, as long as Palestinian ministries face physical, political, and financial barriers, we cannot expect them to be able to fully serve their citizens. In Gaza, Belgium has worked through the Palestinian Authority, and today the situation makes that impossible. Yet our commitment remains firm. When conditions allow, Belgium will be ready to resume its support, because lasting peace demands not only political will, but enduring partnerships and the courage to invest in hope, even when the path is uncertain. Thank you.

Um, Maxime, Maxime, thank you, Belgium, and let me again, it, it is incredibly important that we do not lose sight of the immediate needs that you, uh, of the Palestinian Authority, and, you know, there will be no Palestine, Palestinian state in the long run if it dies, uh, on the way there, so, uh, thank you for that, and, and we are also very… dedicated to that case. Then it is the European Commission, to be followed by Qatar, and I'm honored to give the word to the Commissioner for the Mediterranean, Madame Dubravka Zuceva.

Thank you, Minister. All of us agree that the situation requires urgent international action. I intervene only to support what our HRVP Kaya Kallas already said. So this is something which is very important. So we are always committed to two-state solution. Of course, we were advocating for lasting peace in the region. We also always advocated for the immediate release of all hostages and the protection of Israeli civilians. For us, terrorism cannot be tolerated, so there can be never any place for Hamas, neither now nor in the future. This is something which is evident. But the situation has gone beyond, beyond all limits. So this is what all of us agree. So we strongly condemn the escalation of the situation in Gaza. Of course, there are some numbers here. In the absence of ceasefire, European Union has committed 170 million euro in humanitarian assistance for the Palestine in 2025. So this brings the total European humanitarian aid to 500 million since 2023. Beyond funding, European Union has also transported humanitarian cargo, as you know, through Relief European Union. and supported medical evacuations through the EU Civil Protection Mechanism. UNRWA is currently indispensable, so this year we disbursed 82 million, which was committed this summer. Palestinian Authority, we need reformed, revitalized, modern, and strong Palestinian Authority. So it needs to be given more autonomy and control over its economic, trade, and fiscal policies. This is what we have been doing. So there is a reform agenda with 1.6 billion euros for the next three years. This morning, we signed with European Investment Bank 400 million euro loan. So this is to help small entrepreneurs, small and medium entrepreneurs, and it's about 20,000 small entrepreneurs who will benefit from this 400 million loan. So, but it is important to achieve meaningful progress on the release, what HRVP already said, release by Israel of withheld tax clearance revenues, which they owe to Palestinians. This is something which will help Palestinian Authority. So we have to think about day after in Gaza. As you know, the needs are huge. So this is exactly why the Palestine donor group is being setting up. It will be rooted in the Palestinian reform agenda. The Palestinian Authority will be able to present progress made on reforms to its partners. This is what we expect. And this group will also serve as a forum to facilitate discussions on the recovery and reconstruction of Gaza, once conditions allow, building on the foundations laid out by the Arab plan. This is very important. So the first gathering of this donor Palestinian group should come soon. This is to invite all parties, including the United Nations, and invitations will follow soon. Thank you so much.
Thank you very much, Commissioner. And then I have the honour of giving the floor to Qatar, Mohammed Al-Kulaifi, Minister of State, to be followed by UNRWA.

Honourable Minister, at the outset, I would like to thank the EU, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and Norway for organizing this very important meeting. And to follow the great instruction by our dear minister, I tend not to read from my notes that's pre-prepared, and to be very practical to highlight a few points to take into consideration. We are very much alike when it comes to the major elements of the day after. We believe that the security aspects need to be responded. We believe that there should be an answer for the governance question. We believe that there should be a political horizon when it comes to the Palestinian cause. And we believe that there should be a reconstruction to provide a better life for the Palestinian people. So we're very much alike when it comes to those issues. Of course, more detail need to be integrated. And following up, I think, the very fruitful discussion that some of the Arab and Muslim leaders had with President Trump yesterday, this will pave the way to get a very important stakeholder involved in our serious discussion, which is the United States. And that's something I think is very brings more optimism and hopefulness to the work that we're doing. A few points to take into consideration. Our work will remain ink on paper unless that we reach a ceasefire. And therefore, reaching a ceasefire is something that is extremely critical. Us and our brothers in Egypt, we've been dedicating our time tirelessly and talking to both disputing parties, aiming to reach an agreement. If there is a will, there is a way. Lacking the political will from the disputing parties to a certain areas would damage the whole process. And therefore, I'm being very honest and transparent, pushing a ceasefire and also to something that is extremely important. The parties need to show seriousness toward those issues. We are very much alike, but the right question would be, does the disputing parties are alike when it comes to those very important pillars of the day after? This is something that I think the next days and weeks, we need to invest more time in trying to get the parties to cooperate and be more tolerant towards those process that allows prosperity, peace, and a better life for the people, either in Gaza or the neighborhood. And therefore, I think these are very important elements that we need to take into consideration, it's good that we're benchmarking, it's good that we're learning from previous experiences, DDR, humanitarian assistant, there are a lot of important issues and lesson learned that we can build upon while we go to the details, uh, uh, followed by the, um, very important, um… the adoption of the resolution, the New York resolution here, and that's related to the two-state solution is something that is extremely important. One last point, the recognition of the Palestinian state is a very important step. It is not a symbolic move. It is definitely a pathway towards long-lasting and peaceful solution. We highly encourage the others to continue to follow that path. We will continue to work with our partners in trying to reach that important outcome and to push ceasefire one and also more details into the other important elements. Thank you very much.

Thank you, Mohammed. Thank you, Qatar. And let me also echo what His Highness said, that how much we appreciate the efforts you are doing to provide for a ceasefire, the importance of a ceasefire, and how terribly appalled we were when the very place where ceasefire negotiations were taking place were bombed. in Qatar. So I just want to say from my side as well, but thank you for continuing and thank you for your optimism that the peace is possible. I then have the honor of giving the floor to Philippe Lazarini from Minerva to be followed by Venezuela.

Mr. Chair, we meet as a catastrophic situation in the occupied Palestinian territory threatens the entire region. Evidence is abundant of international crimes perpetrated with the full knowledge of the international community. The government of Israel is implementing a longstanding project to undermine the feasibility of a Palestinian state and separate Palestinians from Palestine. Dismantling UNRWA is a principal element of this agency. It is why the agency has been attacked relentlessly, with 370 colleagues killed, hundreds of premises destroyed, and financial support strangled. The Global Alliance and the New York Declaration envisage a ceasefire, stabilization, Palestinian-led governance, and a just political solution. UNRWA's 30,000-strong workforce, unparalleled service delivery networks, and deep reserves of community trust are key to achieving these goals. The Agency is an indispensable partner for peace. I ask, therefore, that Member States safeguard UNRWA's role within a time-bound political process and finance the provision of essential services until that process is completed. I think, Espen, you keep reminding that there is a risk that the PA might collapse, but if the PA collapse, it will lead onward to the collapse, and if onward collapse, we will also lead the PA to the collapse in the West Bank. So basically, our near future fate is very much intertwined. Thank you.
Thank you very much. I will then give the floor to Venezuela, to be followed by the United Arab Emirates. And the Foreign Minister of Venezuela, Mr. Ivan Gil Pinto, please.

Mr. Chair, we come together today not only as governments, but as human beings. A truly man-made catastrophe that has gone on for far too long. For Each attack on Gaza is not only a wound to Palestinians, but a wound to humanity and to the very foundations of international law. Venezuela stands firmly with Palestine, its people, and their just cause. Venezuela stands firmly with the right of Palestinians to live in freedom and dignity. Mr. Chair. Words of sympathy are not enough. We need real and coordinated action that can yield both meaningful and tangible results. A permanent ceasefire, first and foremost, the swift provision of humanitarian assistance at scale, the withdrawal of Israeli occupying forces, the deployment of a protection force to ensure the safety of the Palestinian people, and a massive international effort to rebuild Gaza under Palestinian leadership. Let us not forget, Palestinians' admission as a full member of the United Nations is not a gesture. It is a recognition of a people's existence, their dignity, and their future. It is a concrete affirmation of the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination. I thank you.

Muchas gracias, Venezuela. I now have the honor of giving the floor to the United Arab Emirates, Minister of State Shaheen, and then to be followed by Portugal.

Please.

Dear Chair, I would like to thank you and express my appreciation for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the European Commission, and also we thank the government of Norway for all the effort they exert in leading this coalition. We have also, UAE has contributed last year in the convention in Riyadh, and also we declare our adoption for the Declaration of New York, which paves the roadway to shape an independent Palestinian state that would live in peace and prosperity near the state of Israel. Now we started working we started implementing the practical steps in order to reach that goal. We welcome the multiple declarations of the state of Palestine, and we invite all the nations that have not accepted that declaration to accept it. When it comes down to the escalations taking place in Gaza and the West Bank, we ask for a ceasefire and for the release of all hostages and to allow the flow of humanitarian aid without restrictions. We support all the negotiation and mediation efforts done by Qatar, Egypt, and the United States, and we invite the Security Council to hold Israel account for all the violations in the occupied Palestine. Over the past decades, we have have made known that there's not going to be a sustainable solution for the state for Palestine without a two-state solution. Therefore, we ask for everybody to contribute to reaching that solution, and at the end, we would like to take this historical moment to make implement tangible measures in order to reach solution and stability long term in the region. And I would like to thank you, Mr. Chair.

For your intervention from the United Arab Emirates. I now have the honor of giving the floor to Portugal to be followed by Switzerland. So it's, uh, Deputy Minister Ana Isabel Xavier from, uh, Portugal.

Thank you, Mr. Chair. Um, allow me to commend to organizers of this very timely meeting of the Global Alliance for the Implementation of the Two-State Solution. For peace between Israelis and Palestinians to stand a chance, concrete and urgent action is needed to indeed finally ensure the implementation of the two-state solution, whereby two independent, sovereign, and democratic states, Israel and Palestine, live side by side in peace and security. As you are aware, Portugal formally recognized the State of Palestine last Sunday, a decision that reflects our long-standing position on the question of Palestine and the two-state solution, a step which seeks to contribute to a just and lasting peace in the Middle East. Portugal will remain actively engaged in all possible ways towards the two-state solution, including in the framework of the Global Alliance. Since its inception, we have always regarded this initiative as a much-needed political and consensus-building forum. The time has come to translate the broad international consensus on the two-state solution into decisive irreversible action. First and foremost, we believe the violence against civilians and the unfathomable human suffering in Gaza must come to an immediate end with a sustainable ceasefire, the immediate resumption of full delivery of humanitarian assistance, and the release of all hostages. Portugal will continue to support UNRWA in its indispensable role in providing humanitarian aid and social services to Palestinians. We have also undertaken to scale up medical treatment of patients from Gaza. Thus, alongside another 26 other countries, we undersigned a joint statement on 23 September on to offer to assist with treatments of patients from Gaza into occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem. Likewise, together with our EU partners, we are committed to increasing support to the Palestinian Authority and to assist in strengthening and reforming Palestinian governance. We salute to work development by the eight working groups set up by the high-level conference on the two-state solution and look forward to carrying on working with partners on the implementation of the actions put forward across all the objectives. Thank you very much.
Uh, we then have, we'll give the floor to Switzerland to be followed by UNSC, and then I invite, uh, Deputy State Secretary Thomas Gerber to speak.

Ministers, Excellencies, Switzerland thanks Saudi Arabia, the EU, and Norway for convening this meeting of the Global Alliance. The situation in the Gaza Strip is unbearable. Switzerland calls for an immediate and permanent ceasefire, the unconditional and immediate release of all hostages, and safe, rapid, and unimpeded humanitarian access. As the occupying power, Israel must respect its obligations under international law, including ensuring supplies to the population under its control. in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, settlement expansion, military escalation and settler violence must cease and be subject to investigation. Occupation is illegal and must end, as confirmed by the International Court of Justice. Switzerland firmly rejects the Israeli occupation of Palestinian territory, settlements, annexation and forced displacement. There is no military solution. Two imperatives are central. Strict respect for international law, including humanitarian law and human rights law, to protect civilians, and the restoration of a credible political horizon to achieve, through diplomacy, the two-state solution. Switzerland supports the New York Declaration of the 29th of July, which commits us to concrete steps to end the war in Gaza, implement the two-state solution, and achieve regional integration. Switzerland welcomes the fact that the Global Alliance is presented as an implementing partner and remains willing to provide support to this end. What is needed today are actors capable of creating spaces that foster dialogue, launching processes, and developing concrete solutions for lasting peace. Switzerland has done so in the past and will continue to do so going forward. Switzerland, in particular, supports the efforts to stabilize the Palestinian Authority, whose reform program is essential for the delivery of services and the preservation of peace prospects. We welcome its commitment to these reforms and its intention to return to Gaza, and we are reviewing the various ongoing initiatives aimed at providing the Palestinian Authority with the means to fulfill its ambitions. Switzerland will continue to support these efforts, maintain strong humanitarian action, and place its good offices at the service of dialogue towards the two-state solution. Thank you.
Thank you very much, Switzerland. And then we'll give the floor to UNSCOW, to be followed by Estonia. And I'm happy to give the floor to Mr. Ramiz Alakbarov.

Excellencies, colleagues. extend my appreciation to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the European Union, and Norway for their continued leadership in this forum. This alliance and your efforts over the past year were pivotal in providing the basis for the New York Declaration endorsed by the General Assembly this month, and it gives a blueprint for concrete actions towards the implementation of the two-state solution grounded in international law and UN resolutions. This mission must include a sovereign and independent Palestinian state, existing in peace and security alongside Israel, with Jerusalem as the capital of both states. We also must support Israel's greater regional integration, with both states living in peace and within their secure and internationally recognized borders. Ladies and gentlemen, the possibility of realizing this vision is eroded by unabated devastation of Gaza, the holding of hostages in unbearable condition, regional escalations, and by daily violence, including acts of terror, and settler-related violence, settlement expansion, demolitions, unilateral actions that undermine peace. People on all sides are losing hope in the promise of the two-state solution that can deliver peace, security, and justice. I welcome today's tone of committing to moving from declarations to actions which promote peace, and the realization of the two-state solution. The path is clear, but requires a shift from promises to the actions in the end to the real political will. Important elements here. We must reach an important and a permanent ceasefire and release of all hostages in Gaza. Humanitarian assistance must be scaled up and early recovery started to meet immense needs. And UN is working tirelessly to make it happen, but our resource situation is there. Recovery and reconstruction in Gaza should reinforce the two-state vision with a single Palestinian government that is recognized and supported by the Palestinian people and international community. Supporting Palestinian Authority is an immediate priority. I urge international community to recognize when progress is made and to continue to support Palestinian government and its reform agenda under these incredibly challenging circumstances. It is important that Palestinian people and the international community supports the recognition of the Palestinian government, which governs across all APT, with Gaza and West Bank unified politically, economically, and administratively. The United Nations stands ready to support this effort. I will continue to engage with all parties and with international partners, specifically in the region, to advance this commitment. I thank you for your attention.
Thank you very much to UNSCO. I will then give the floor to Estonia, to be followed by Austria. And Estonia is represented by Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, Minna Lind.

Thank you very much, Minister. It is clear that we must redouble our joint peace efforts and encourage Israeli and Palestinian leaders to move towards mutually acceptable agreements. We need an immediate ceasefire in Gaza, as has been said already in this room many times. The suffering of civilians, including children, is absolutely heartbreaking. And the confirmation of famine should serve as another stark wake-up call. It is vital that the UN and humanitarian partners have access and operate safely in Gaza in line with international humanitarian law. Estonia has provided humanitarian assistance through international humanitarian organizations, and furthermore, Estonian refugee aid is providing food aid to several hospitals in Gaza City to support both patients and healthcare workers there. Estonia believes that a genuine two-state solution, grounded in international law and the UN resolutions, remains the only viable path to a just and durable peace. Both peoples deserve the right to live in secure, sovereign states, side by side, free from violence and fear. We have endorsed the New York Declaration on the two-state solution and hope it will give renewed momentum to its implementation. We will continue to support the Palestinian Authority and its reform agenda. We know that the task before us is immense, but hopefully not insurmountable. Thank you.
Thank you very much to Estonia. I then have the honour of giving the floor to Austria, to be followed by Finland. So the Deputy Minister of Austria, please.

Thank you, Mr. President, Ministers, Excellencies, dear colleagues. These recent months have only strengthened our conviction that the two-state solution remains the only viable path to peace. As a first and crucial steps towards resuming a credible peace process, the war in Gaza must end. The ceasefire must go hand in hand with the immediate and unconditional release of all remaining hostages by Hamas. Furthermore, Hamas must lay down its weapons and must not be playing any role in a post-war scenario. The humanitarian situation in Gaza is unacceptable. The suffering of the civilian population must stop. Since the outbreak of hostilities, Austria has provided over 67 million euros in humanitarian assistance to Gaza and to the conflict-ridden region. It is important to enable UN agencies that play a key role in aid distribution to do their job. Austria reaffirms its support for a two-state solution. For this reason, Austria has signed the New York Declaration and supported the UN resolution endorsing the document. Austria will remain a principled, constructive, and reliable partner in this alliance. We will continue to use our relationships and contacts to all sides to advance dialogue and trust, and we will continue supporting the Palestinian Authority in its reform efforts. In conclusion, let me reiterate that we stand ready to work with the European, Israeli, Arab, and other international partners to create the conditions for a viable peace process, one that delivers security, dignity, and prosperity for Israelis and Palestinians alike. Thank you.

Thank you very much to Austria. Also, thank you for being part of this and having signed the declaration. That's really much appreciated. I will now give the floor to Finland, to be followed by Denmark. And Finland is represented by Deputy Minister Outi Hopoainen.

Chairs, Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, Finland commends France and Saudi Arabia for their vision and leadership at this critical moment, and we thank everyone in this hall for their commitment to this cause. To create a foundation for a lasting peace, the legitimate rights of both Israelis and Palestinians must be secured. The right to live in peace and security, and to pursue economic, social, and cultural development. Excellencies, as we know, the path to peace is not easy. But as our former president, the Nobel laureate Martti Ahtisaari put it, it is a matter of will. Beyond that, what we need right now is, firstly, an unconditional and permanent ceasefire in Gaza, the release of all hostages, and no restrictions on the flow of humanitarian aid. This will help us go beyond the most immediate concerns. Secondly, the Palestinian Authority must have the financial means to develop the Palestinian society. This will help the Palestinian institutions get on their feet, which is what is needed to create a strong Palestinian state. And we note the new initiative of the Palestine Donor Group. Thirdly, and here I refer to the intervention by Luxembourg, Israel's security must also be fully ensured. The process at hand must also bring further recognitions of the State of Israel in the region. This will ensure that the peace will last. We know that education is the backbone of society. Finland has supported education sector in Palestine for years, and the learning outcomes have been among the best in the region, high literacy and school enrollment rates being a proof of this. Ladies and gentlemen, Finland is firmly committed to the two-state solution and stands ready to continue to do its part.
Thank you, Minister Holopainen. Then it is Denmark, to be followed by France. I give the floor to Under-Secretary Eva-Maria Frieda Barloes.

Thank you, Excellencies. Denmark fully supports the Global Alliance as a platform for creating momentum behind a peaceful solution to the conflict. As others have said, the war in Gaza needs to stop. As a current member of the UN Security Council and EU presidency, Denmark continues to push for an immediate and permanent ceasefire, unconditional release of all hostages, and unhindered humanitarian access to Gaza. The reconstruction of Gaza will be an enormous task for the international community, which we need to prepare for. It will require a coordinated effort with the Palestinian Authority in a leading role. We reiterate that Hamas can have no future role in Gaza. Denmark is ready to play a role in the efforts of early recovery and reconstruction of Gaza as soon as the situation on the ground permits. We need to see a return of the PA to Gaza with the whole of Palestine unified under one political leadership. Reform of the PA is a necessary condition along the path to a credible Palestinian state. Denmark has been an active voice in the EU in promoting support for capacity building and reform of the PA. We are proud to join the emergency coalition and to contribute with emergency support for the Palestinian Authority. Now this week, we really have witnessed a renewed energy and enthusiasm for peace based on the two-state solution, a solution that Denmark is very much prepared to build on. This is why the Danish Minister of Foreign Affairs stated on Monday that the keys to recognition of a Palestinian state should no longer lie in the hands of the Israeli government. The Palestinians themselves must become masters of their own destiny. At this critical juncture and through this meeting today, we must do everything in our power to support that.
Thank you. Thank you, Denmark. I will now give the floor to France, to be followed by the United Kingdom. And from France, represented by Director Romaric Rognan.

I want to thank the European Union, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and Norway for convening. this new meeting of the Global Alliance. I believe this format gathers countries that are both horrified by the unjustifiable humanitarian toll that the continuing war in Gaza brings, but also believe that international law, negotiation between the parties, regional integration and cooperation should be the foundation of a solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Earlier this week, with the two-state solution and the New York Declaration, we achieved a key milestone, I believe, in fostering international consensus and reaffirming the centrality of the two-state solution as the cornerstone of the solution. I'm proud to stand as a representative of a country which decided to recognize the state of Palestine as the vindication of the Palestinian people right for self-determination. We also fostered through this conference international consensus on what should come after, what should come next, a ceasefire, liberation of all stages, unhindered humanitarian access, removal of Hamas from governance of Gaza and disarmament, and the need for stabilization mission. We believe also that the Global Alliance has a key role to play to keep the international mobilization alive and active as the follow-up mechanism of the New York Declaration. We also welcome the discussions that took place yesterday between the U.S. and a number of Arab and Muslim countries. which are an opportunity to prevent further escalation through annexation or settlement acceleration. And finally, I would like to have a message for the Palestinian Authority, which has come up with courageous reforms commitment within the context of the two-state solution conference. And as we work with the PA to ensure accountability, transparency, and efficiency in their implementation, We also need to step up our support to the PA, both financial and political, and this is why we have joined with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Spain, and Norway in a call to join our efforts and step up our efforts in this regard. Thank you very much.

Thank you very much to France, and also thank you for reminding us about that immediate task that we have to work on together. And it's open for more countries if they want to join in raising the budget support for the PA in this current situation. I will now, if it's okay with Germany, I will now switch UK and Germany. So if Christian Buch is ready, Director General for Political Affairs, and then UK. Is that okay?

Thank you, Chair. High Representative, Ministers, Excellencies, colleagues, Germany subscribes to the New York Declaration. We voted for the resolution endorsing it. This declaration guides us in this week and beyond. It is our firm conviction that only a two-state solution with a Palestinian state existing side by side in peace and security with Israel will guarantee peace in the region and Israel's existence as a Jewish and democratic state. We believe that all peoples in the region have the right to live without fear and in dignity. This is a message that we convey on an almost daily basis to our Israeli friends. The two-state solution is the only way out of this conflict. For that very reason, it is our clear policy to protect the viability of the two-state solution. We push back against any attempt to weaken or destroy it. for instance by withholding tax revenues which belong to the Palestinian people. We reject settlements and any thoughts of annexation. And it is for this very reason that we contribute every single day in cash and in kind to building the foundations and institutions of a Palestinian state. Germany's current development cooperation with the PA amounts to more than 1 billion U.S. dollars, tens of billions since Oslo. Ladies and gentlemen, joint narratives for peace for the two-state solution are more important than ever.
